topic: Morning and evening phone use as cognitive frame
body:
**Your first interaction of the day is with your phone. Your last one is too. And you have tried to change that more times than you can count.**

Here is why it keeps failing. You are treating it as a motivation problem — trying harder not to reach for it. But the phone is on your nightstand. It is physically the closest object to you in the two moments when your cognitive defences are lowest — just waking and just before sleep.

The morning matters more. The first 60 minutes after waking is a neurologically distinct window. Your brain is primed for absorption, not analysis. Whatever you put in front of it in that window sets the attentional tone for the rest of the day.

Put a feed of notifications and performance metrics in front of it — you have started your day in reactive mode. Someone else's agenda is already running in your head before your own priorities have loaded.

The phone is not the problem. The nightstand is.

Move it tonight. Charger in the kitchen, the hallway, anywhere that requires you to stand up and walk to get to it. The extra steps are not inconvenient — they are the mechanism. Friction is the system.

Protect the morning window. Everything else compounds from there.

Link in bio for the morning protocol in full.
